Container.Name: mcpelevator
Container.Overview:
Elevate MCP servers into authenticated HTTP endpoints - self-hosted, in one container. Most MCP servers ship as stdio programs (npx/uvx commands) that phones and remote clients can't spawn. mcpelevator runs them for you and exposes each as a remote Streamable HTTP endpoint that Claude mobile (or any MCP client) on your network can connect to: add a server in the web UI, press start, copy the URL. Batteries included (Node/npx + Python/uv preinstalled), with process supervision, live logs, a registry browser for one-click installs, bearer-token auth, and a Host/Origin guard. Already-remote MCP servers can be proxied behind the same auth too.
DOCKER RUNNER (advanced, opt-in): mcpelevator can also run MCP servers packaged as Docker images. It is OFF by default and ROOT-EQUIVALENT - to use it, set the Docker Runner variable to true AND manually add a Path mapping /var/run/docker.sock -> /var/run/docker.sock. See the Unraid guide for the walkthrough.
FIRST LOGIN: this template enables LAN access, which turns control-plane auth on - the admin token is minted on first start and printed ONCE to the container log. Open the log, copy the token, and log in at http://[unraid-ip]:8080. Host networking is used so the LAN-access gate sees real client IPs (with bridge + port publishing every client would look like the Docker gateway). Full guide: https://github.com/pacnpal/mcpelevator/blob/main/docs/unraid.md

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port the control plane binds on the host. Host networking has no port mapping, so this variable IS the host port - change it if 8080 is already taken, and update the container's WebUI field to match so the WebUI link keeps working.

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: Persistent data: SQLite database (servers, tokens, settings) and the npm/uv package caches so installed MCP servers survive restarts.

Config.Name: Allow LAN Access
Config.Description: First-boot seed for the 'allow access from devices on your local network' setting, so this headless box is reachable at http://[unraid-ip]:8080 right away. Enabling it turns control-plane auth ON: the admin token is printed ONCE to the container log on first start - copy it there to log in. Only seeds the first boot; the toggle in Settings is authoritative afterwards.

Config.Name: Admin Token (break-glass)
Config.Description: Optional. A control-plane token that is always accepted on /api. Leave empty normally (a token is minted and printed to the log on first start); set it to recover from a lost token or for automation, then remove it.

Config.Name: Public Base URL
Config.Description: Optional. Absolute URL clients use to reach this instance when it sits behind a tunnel or reverse proxy (e.g. https://mcp.example.com). The copy menu hands out endpoint URLs based on it, and its hostname is trusted by the Host/Origin guard.

Config.Name: Extra Allowed Hosts
Config.Description: Optional. Comma-separated extra hostnames the Host/Origin guard always trusts (e.g. a reverse-proxy hostname that resolves to this box). Not needed for plain LAN access by IP.

Config.Name: Docker Runner (root-equivalent)
Config.Description: OPT-IN and ROOT-EQUIVALENT. First-boot seed for the docker runner, which launches MCP servers packaged as Docker images on a mounted Docker daemon. Anything that can reach the Docker socket is effectively root on the host, so enable this only if you trust every image you run. To use it, you must ALSO add a Path mount manually (click 'Add another Path, Port, Variable...' at the bottom of this page) with Container Path and Host Path both set to /var/run/docker.sock (sibling-container model) - or point mcpelevator at a separate dind daemon via a DOCKER_HOST variable instead. OFF by default; the Settings toggle is authoritative after first boot.

Config.Name: Mint Admin Token On Boot
Config.Description: Recovery hatch: set to true to mint a fresh admin token on boot and print it to the container log (existing tokens keep working). Set back to false after grabbing it, or a new token is minted on every restart.

Config.Name: Max Running Servers
Config.Description: Cap on concurrently running MCP servers.

Config.Name: Start Timeout (seconds)
Config.Description: Readiness timeout per server start - generous by default to cover npx/uvx cold-start package installs. Raise it for very large packages.
